chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdillah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from some of his teachers, who said:

A woman said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or a man asked him about a man whose wife claims he has 'unna' (impotence/inability to consummate), and the man denies it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The midwife should insert the salve (khalooq) into her, and the man does not know. If it comes out and the salve is on his penis, she is truthful and he is lying; otherwise, she is lying and he is truthful.'

key_terms.الْخَلُوقُ: A medicinal salve or ointment used for verification
key_terms.صَدَقَتْ: She is truthful (her claim is accepted)
key_terms.عُنَّةٌ: Impotence or inability to consummate marriage
key_terms.كَذَبَتْ: She is lying (her claim is rejected)

ai.seo_question: How is impotence (unna) legally verified in Shia jurisprudence when husband and wife disagree?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar details a practical forensic method used in Shia jurisprudence to resolve disputes over 'unna' (impotence) by using a sticky salve (khalooq) to leave a physical trace during intercourse. It highlights the reliance on empirical evidence and the testimony of a midwife (qabala) to verify the husband's physical capability, serving as a key precedent for marital dispute resolution in fiqh.
